messages.subject: Re: Problem with the sfit package
parts:
Hi.

Ok, the 'cfit' executable was created and seems to work. The problem
is that R for some reason cannot "run" it. More troubleshooting -
what do you get in the following cases, with the 'cfit' executable in
the current directory:

> print(capabilities())

> print(getOption("encoding"))

> con <- pipe("ls -1")
> print(con)

> print(readLines(con))

> pwd <- getwd()
> print(pwd)

> print(dir())

> system("cfit")

> con2 <- pipe("cfit")
> print(con2)

> print(readLines(con2))

> pathname <- file.path(pwd, "cfit")
> print(pathname)

> print(file.info(pathname))

> system(pathname)

> con3 <- pipe(pathname)
> print(con3)

> print(readLines(con3))


/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: Problem with the sfit package
parts:
Hi,

try this:

> library(sfit)
> source("http://www.braju.com/R/patches/sfit/20070520/fix.R")
> print(getOption("cfit"))
> readLines(pipe(getOption("cfit")))

If it works, try:

> example(cfit.matrix)

Does it work? If it does, do the above source() and the allelic
crosstalk calibration should work. Before updating the sfit package,
I will have to validate that the patch works on other platforms too.

/Henrik

PS. Please use "reply to all". DS.

-M, --outM <filename>     where M is dumped [ stdout ]

    --QRtolerance <num>   ratio of ||q_i||/||q_1|| (QR termination)

-C, --constraints  <int>  0 none, 1 nonnegative, 2 box, 3 probability-like
-x, --lubox <lb,ub>       lower and upper bound in box constraints
                          (specifying this turns on --constraints 2). If this
                          is not specified, the dimension-specific lower and
                          upper bounds are read from a file `lubox' containing
                          2 x m  matrix of lower- and upper-bound vectors.

-o, --origin <filename>   origin vector, offset data by this vector [default 0]
-g, --gamma <num>        `eye-height' in projective transform [default 0]
-u, --viewdir <filename> `viewing direction' vector [ meanY/(meanY^T meanY) ]
    --u_1T                u = (1,1,1,... )
-D, --denom_weight        use the denominators as observation weights
    --outPY <filename>    save the transformed Y into this file
    --outPM <filename>    dump projective-transformed M (according
                          to the dump mode option).

-Q, --chopmore <num>      or more than the specified percentiles.

-R, --robust <num>        robust coefficient (if compiled with -DWITH_ROBUST)
character(0)
>

Now the example from cfit.matrix works!
> example(cfit.matrix)

cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cft.mt> # Simulate data
cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cft.mt> N <- 1000

cft.mt> # Simulate genotypes
cft.mt> g <- sample(c("AA", "AB", "AB", "BB"), size=N, replace=TRUE)

cft.mt> # Simulate concentrations of allele A and allele B
cft.mt> X <- matrix(rexp(N), nrow=N, ncol=2)

cft.mt> colnames(X) <- c("A", "B")

cft.mt> X[g == "AA", "B"] <- 0

cft.mt> X[g == "BB", "A"] <- 0

cft.mt> X[g == "AB",] <- X[g == "AB",] / 2

cft.mt> # Transform noisy X
cft.mt> xi <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)

cft.mt> a0 <- c(0,0)+0.3

cft.mt> A <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.8), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)

cft.mt> A <- apply(A, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))

cft.mt> Z <- t(a0 + A %*% t(X + xi))

cft.mt> # Add noise to Y
cft.mt> eps <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)

cft.mt> Y <- Z + eps

cft.mt> layout(matrix(1:4, ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))

cft.mt> xlab <- "Allele A"

cft.mt> ylab <- "Allele B"

cft.mt> lim <- c(0,6)

cft.mt> plot(X, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim)

cft.mt> points(Z, col="blue")

cft.mt> points(Y, col="red")

cft.mt> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2, legend=c("X", "Z", "Y"), col=c("black", "blue", "red"), title="Variables:", bg="#eeeeee")

cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cft.mt> # Fit model
cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cft.mt> alpha <- c(0.10, 0.075, 0.05, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001)

cft.mt> fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98)

cft.mt> Ms <- fit$M

cft.mt> col <- terrain.colors(length(Ms))

cft.mt> #col <- rainbow(length(Ms))
cft.mt> col[length(Ms)] <- "red"

cft.mt> lim <- c(-0.5,5)

cft.mt> plot(Y, cex=0.8, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim, main="Y")

cft.mt> for (kk in seq(along=Ms)) {
cft.mt+   M <- Ms[[kk]]
cft.mt+   points(M, pch=19, cex=2.5, col=col[kk])
cft.mt+   lines(M, col=col[kk], lwd=2)
cft.mt+   text(M, cex=0.8, labels=kk)
cft.mt+ }

cft.mt> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2, legend=c(alpha, "final"), col=col, title=expression(alpha), bg="#eeeeee")

cft.mt> apex <- which.min(apply(M, MARGIN=1, FUN=function(u) sum(u^2)))

cft.mt> a0hat <- M[apex,]

cft.mt> Ahat <- M[-apex,]

cft.mt> Ahat <- apply(Ahat, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))

cft.mt> if (sum(Ahat[c(1,4)]^2) < sum(Ahat[c(2,3)]^2)) {
cft.mt+   Ahat <- matrix(Ahat[c(2,1,4,3)], nrow=2)
cft.mt+ }

cft.mt> Ainv <- solve(Ahat)

cft.mt> Xhat <- t(Ainv %*% (t(Y) - a0hat))

cft.mt> cat("True A:\n")
True A:

cft.mt> print(A)
          [,1]      [,2]
[1,] 0.9938837 0.1240347
[2,] 0.1104315 0.9922779

cft.mt> cat("Estimated A:\n")
Estimated A:

cft.mt> print(Ahat)
            V1        V2
[1,] 0.9873211 0.1216088
[2,] 0.1587355 0.9925781

cft.mt> plot(Xhat, cex=0.8, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim, main=expression(hat(X)))

cft.mt> x1 <- par("usr")[2]

cft.mt> y1 <- par("usr")[4]

cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,x1), y=c(0,0), col="red", lwd=2)

cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,0), y=c(0,y1), col="red", lwd=2)

cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,x1), y=c(0,y1), col="blue", lwd=2)

cft.mt> plot(X[,1], Xhat[,1], cex=0.8, xlab=expression(X), ylab=expression(hat(X)), xlim=lim, ylim=lim)

cft.mt> points(X[,2], Xhat[,2], cex=0.8, col="red")

cft.mt> abline(a=0, b=1, lwd=2)
>

allelic crosstalk calibration now works without any warnings or errors.

cheers

Lavinia

messages.subject: Re: Problem with the sfit package
parts:
Hi,

I've just committed a new version of the sfit package that fixes the
problem below that might occur on some Unix systems. Just do:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
hbLite("aroma.affymetrix")

and that should update all packages including sfit.

Cheers

Henrik
On 5/20/07, Lavinia Gordon <lavinia...@mcri.edu.au> wrote:

> Following these guidelines:
>
> At 08:40 PM 20/05/2007 -0700, Henrik Bengtsson wrote:
>
> library(sfit)
> source("http://www.braju.com/R/patches/sfit/20070520/fix.R")
> print(getOption("cfit"))
> readLines(pipe(getOption("cfit")))
> > library(sfit)
> Loading required package: R.oo
> R.oo v1.2.7 (2006-04-07) successfully loaded. See ?R.oo for help.
> sfit v0.1.1 (2006-05-20) successfully loaded. See ?sfit for help.
> >
> source("http://www.braju.com/R/patches/sfit/20070520/fix.R")
> Warning message:
> Method already existed and was overwritten: cfit.matrix in:
> setMethodS3.default("cfit", "matrix", function(y, k = ncol(y) +
> > print(getOption("cfit"))
> [1] "\"/usr/local/lib/R/library/sfit/bin/cfit\""
> > readLines(pipe(getOption("cfit")))
>
> cfit [ options ] k [ data [ weight ]]
>
> Fit a simplex with k vertices to points in the file <data> (stdin
> is used if not supplied).
>
> <weight> is a file of point weights (if not supplied, w_j = 1/n).
>
> -h, --help this help
> -v, --verbose dump progress to stderr
>
> -i, --Minit <filename> initial simplex
> -d, --dump <int> dump mode (0 none, 1 final, 2 each alpha, 3 each
> REX)
> -M, --outM <filename> where M is dumped [ stdout ]
> -X, --outX <filename> where X is dumped
>
> -a, --alpha <num,num,...> comma- or space-separated sequence of alpha
> -T, --maxiter <int> maximum number of REX steps
> -f, --frobratio <num> ratio of ||DM||/||M|| (inner loop convergence)
> --QRtolerance <num> ratio of ||q_i||/||q_1|| (QR termination)
>
> -C, --constraints <int> 0 none, 1 nonnegative, 2 box, 3 probability-like
> -x, --lubox <lb,ub> lower and upper bound in box constraints
> (specifying this turns on --constraints 2). If
> this
> is not specified, the dimension-specific lower
> and
> upper bounds are read from a file `lubox'
> containing
> 2 x m matrix of lower- and upper-bound vectors.
>
> -o, --origin <filename> origin vector, offset data by this vector
> [default 0]
> -g, --gamma <num> `eye-height' in projective transform [default 0]
> -u, --viewdir <filename> `viewing direction' vector [ meanY/(meanY^T meanY)
> ]
> --u_1T u = (1,1,1,... )
> -D, --denom_weight use the denominators as observation weights
> --outPY <filename> save the transformed Y into this file
> --outPM <filename> dump projective-transformed M (according
> to the dump mode option).
>
> -q, --chopless <num> assign zero weight to points if u^T y is less
> -Q, --chopmore <num> or more than the specified percentiles.
>
> -R, --robust <num> robust coefficient (if compiled with
> -DWITH_ROBUST)
> character(0)
> >
>
> Now the example from cfit.matrix works!
> > example(cfit.matrix)
>
> cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
> - -
> cft.mt> # Simulate data
> cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
> - -
> cft.mt> N <- 1000
>
> cft.mt> # Simulate genotypes
> cft.mt> g <- sample(c("AA", "AB", "AB", "BB"), size=N, replace=TRUE)
>
> cft.mt> # Simulate concentrations of allele A and allele B
> cft.mt> X <- matrix(rexp(N), nrow=N, ncol=2)
>
> cft.mt> colnames(X) <- c("A", "B")
>
> cft.mt> X[g == "AA", "B"] <- 0
>
> cft.mt> X[g == "BB", "A"] <- 0
>
> cft.mt> X[g == "AB",] <- X[g == "AB",] / 2
>
> cft.mt> # Transform noisy X
> cft.mt> xi <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)
>
> cft.mt> a0 <- c(0,0)+0.3
>
> cft.mt> A <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.8), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
>
> cft.mt> A <- apply(A, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))
>
> cft.mt> Z <- t(a0 + A %*% t(X + xi))
>
> cft.mt> # Add noise to Y
> cft.mt> eps <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)
>
> cft.mt> Y <- Z + eps
>
> cft.mt> layout(matrix(1:4, ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))
>
> cft.mt> xlab <- "Allele A"
>
> cft.mt> ylab <- "Allele B"
>
> cft.mt> lim <- c(0,6)
>
> cft.mt> plot(X, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim)
>
> cft.mt> points(Z, col="blue")
>
> cft.mt> points(Y, col="red")
>
> cft.mt> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2, legend=c("X", "Z", "Y"),
> col=c("black", "blue", "red"), title="Variables:", bg="#eeeeee")
>
> cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
> - -
> cft.mt> # Fit model
> cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
> - -
> cft.mt> alpha <- c(0.10, 0.075, 0.05, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001)
>
> cft.mt> fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98)
>
> cft.mt> Ms <- fit$M
>
> cft.mt> col <- terrain.colors(length(Ms))
>
> cft.mt> #col <- rainbow(length(Ms))
> cft.mt> col[length(Ms)] <- "red"
>
> cft.mt> lim <- c(-0.5,5)
>
> cft.mt> plot(Y, cex=0.8, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim,
> main="Y")
>
> cft.mt> for (kk in seq(along=Ms)) {
> cft.mt+ M <- Ms[[kk]]
> cft.mt+ points(M, pch=19, cex=2.5, col=col[kk])
> cft.mt+ lines(M, col=col[kk], lwd=2)
> cft.mt+ text(M, cex=0.8, labels=kk)
> cft.mt+ }
>
> cft.mt> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2, legend=c(alpha, "final"),
> col=col, title=expression(alpha), bg="#eeeeee")
>
> cft.mt> apex <- which.min(apply(M, MARGIN=1, FUN=function(u) sum(u^2)))
>
> cft.mt> a0hat <- M[apex,]
>
> cft.mt> Ahat <- M[-apex,]
>
> cft.mt> Ahat <- apply(Ahat, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))
>
> cft.mt> if (sum(Ahat[c(1,4)]^2) < sum(Ahat[c(2,3)]^2)) {
> cft.mt+ Ahat <- matrix(Ahat[c(2,1,4,3)], nrow=2)
> cft.mt+ }
>
> cft.mt> Ainv <- solve(Ahat)
>
> cft.mt> Xhat <- t(Ainv %*% (t(Y) - a0hat))
>
> cft.mt> cat("True A:\n")
> True A:
>
> cft.mt> print(A)
> [,1] [,2]

> [2,] 0.1104315 0.9922779

> cft.mt> y1 <- par("usr")[4]

> cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,x1), y=c(0,0), col="red", lwd=2)
>
> cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,0), y=c(0,y1), col="red", lwd=2)
>
> cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,x1), y=c(0,y1), col="blue", lwd=2)
>
> cft.mt> plot(X[,1], Xhat[,1], cex=0.8, xlab=expression(X),
> ylab=expression(hat(X)), xlim=lim, ylim=lim)
>
> cft.mt> points(X[,2], Xhat[,2], cex=0.8, col="red")
